summary: ```# 【Marvelous Designer】Half-Skirt Production Tutorial - Uniform Skirt, Pumpkin Skirt, Pencil Skirt, etc. p03 3_Tail Skirt ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to create the tail of the fish for our skirt design. This process involves several steps that ensure the tail is proportionate and visually appealing in relation to the skirt body. ## Adjusting the Tail of the Fish To begin, we will use the method introduced in the first video. Since the tail of the fish is relatively close to the body, we need to adjust its position slightly inward and downward to achieve a cohesive look. 1. **Select and Move**: Select the two sides of the tail and move them. - **Tip**: Hold the SHIFT key while moving to constrain the movement along the horizontal or vertical direction. - **Goal**: Position the tail closer to the knee. ## Creating the Back Panel Next, we will focus on the back panel of the skirt. 1. **Select and Rotate**: Select the back panel and rotate it around the Y-axis to align with the center line. 2. **Use Rectangle Tool**: Click and drag in the 2D window using the rectangle tool to match the width of the skirt. 3. **Draw Length Panel**: Utilize the 2D scale to create a length panel. 4. **Symmetrical Panel Creation**: Select the panel and press `CTRL + D` to create a symmetrical counterpart. 5. **Copy and Paste**: Copy and paste a group to serve as the back panel. 6. **Adjust Width**: If the back panel appears too wide, manually adjust it. 7. **Arrange Panels**: Press `SHIFT + F` to open the arrangement point and position the four panels accordingly. ## Assembling the Skirt After arranging the panels, we can proceed with the assembly. 1. **Sewing Panels**: Use the rectangle tool to connect the top and bottom panels, ensuring the sides are also sewn together. 2. **Visual Inspection**: At this stage, the assembled panels should resemble a traditional skirt. ## Utilizing the Extension Tool We will now apply the extension tool to enhance the design. 1. **Finding the Tool**: In the Edit panel tool group, locate the extension tool (second column). 2. **Creating Fold Lines**: - Click on the top center point, then the bottom center point to create a fold line. - The fold line can be opened outward to create a fan shape. 3. **Adjusting Folds**: After creating the extension reference line, select the left and right sides to adjust the fan shape. - If necessary, click on the line to open both sides simultaneously. ## Adjusting Fan Lines and Curves To ensure a smooth finish, we need to refine the fan lines. 1. **Separating Panels**: In the 2D window, slightly separate the panels to create space for additional fan lines. 2. **Tightening at the Knee**: Adjust the lines below to bring both points inward for a tighter fit at the knee. 3. **Length Adjustment**: Select the line and right-click to change the length, ensuring both sides are selected. - Set the length to match the bottom panel of the top panel. ## Final Adjustments If more folds are needed: 1. **Opening Panels**: Continue to extend the panels as necessary. 2. **Smoothing Curves**: Convert points to free curve points for easier adjustments. Use the editor curve point tool to delete excess points and retain only the necessary ones. 3. **Ensuring Smoothness**: While adjusting, maintain a smooth curve without sharp angles. ## Sewing and Top-Stitching 1. **Avoiding Missing Pieces**: Ensure all corners are smooth to avoid any missing segments during sewing. 2. **Final Top-Stitch**: Adjust the curve carefully, ensuring the top-stitch is placed centrally without visible seams. The curve should start from the top for a clean finish. ## Conclusion Once all adjustments are made, we will have successfully completed the top-stitch. At this point, we can revisit the other side of the design for any additional tweaks or refinements. ```
